h1:
Nong Khai to Loei: Chiang Khan
3 Days Along the Mekong
intro: If you're already in Nong Khai and want to stretch the trip out, drive west along the Mekong on Route 211. This road takes you out of Nong Khai town, through Tha Bo, Si Chiang Mai and Sangkhom, then crosses into Loei province and ends in Chiang Khan. The Mekong hugs the road for almost the whole way, with cliffside temples, waterfalls, mountain viewpoints, and an old riverside town to round it off, all in one trip. We've laid it out as a relaxed 3 days and 2 nights driving yourself, with no rush and plenty of stops to take photos and eat along the way.

blocks.html: This trip works best if you have your own car or rent one to drive yourself, because public transport along the Route 211 riverside is sparse and the stops are spread out. The total distance from Nong Khai town to Chiang Khan is around 200 km, and driving it straight through takes about three and a half hours. But the whole appeal of this road is in the stops, so we've broken it into 3 days: one night on the road near Sangkhom, then one more night in Chiang Khan.

blocks.text: The route and how to prepare

items: Main route — Highway 211 along the Mekong: Nong Khai → Tha Bo → Si Chiang Mai → Sangkhom → Pak Chom (Loei) → Chiang Khan
Road conditions — two lanes in stretches, with bends and climbs around Sangkhom–Pak Chom. Driving in daylight is safer; avoid driving at night since street lighting is minimal
Fuel — fill up in Nong Khai town or Si Chiang Mai, as big stations are far apart on the Sangkhom–Pak Chom stretch
Best time to go — November to February is cool, with a good chance of a sea of fog at Wat Pha Tak Suea and Phu Tok. The Mekong drops to show its rapids and sandbars clearly around February to May

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Route 211 really is beautiful, but it's no expressway, so don't set out to drive fast. Leave plenty of time to stop and shoot photos at the roadside viewpoints. And if you go in the rainy season, the waterfalls run hard and look great, but the climbs up to the hilltop temples can get slippery, so wear shoes with decent grip.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Leaving Nong Khai, along the Mekong to Sangkhom

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Nong Khai → Tha Bo → Si Chiang Mai → Sangkhom

items.activity: Leave Nong Khai town, fill up the tank, and grab water and snacks for the road
items.note: Have breakfast in town before you head out. That first meal matters because the morning drive is a long one

items.activity: Pass through Tha Bo, a small riverside town. Stop for a few river-view photos and pick up the local pla som (fermented fish) and naem that Tha Bo is known for
items.note: Tha Bo is an old center for making pla som, so it's worth buying some to take home

items.activity: Reach Sangkhom and head up to Wat Pha Tak Suea to walk the glass Skywalk that juts out from the cliff, looking down on the winding Mekong
items.note: The Skywalk admits one group at a time and you have to wear the cloth foot covers provided at the entrance. Entry is just a few tens of baht, and mornings give you a shot at the fog

items.activity: Come down from the hill and find lunch at a riverside restaurant in Sangkhom town. Order fried Mekong fish and larb
items.note: Fresh Mekong river fish is the local specialty on this road. A plate runs around 120–200 THB depending on the size of the fish

items.activity: Stop at Than Thong Waterfall inside the arboretum for a walk and a cool-off in the water
items.note: It's not a big waterfall but it's shady, a nice place to stretch your legs after a long drive. In the rainy season the water runs harder and looks better than in the dry months

items.activity: Check in to a riverside place around Sangkhom, drop your bags, and sit by the water for sunset
items.note: Riverside places in Sangkhom range from small resorts to homestays, around 600–1,500 THB/night. Book ahead in the cool season

items.activity: Dinner by the river, quiet, with the sound of the water, an easy end to day one
items.note: Restaurants in Sangkhom close fairly early, so if you want dinner, order before 8 pm

blocks.text: Day 2 — From Sangkhom into Loei, overnight in Chiang Khan

items.activity: Have breakfast at your place, then carry on along Route 211 heading into Loei province
items.note: The Sangkhom–Pak Chom stretch climbs and dips along the Mekong and is one of the prettiest parts of the trip. Drive slowly and pull over to shoot photos at the roadside viewpoints

items.activity: Pass through Pak Chom in Loei. Stop at a riverside viewpoint and take a restroom break
items.note: Pak Chom is the junction before you enter the Chiang Khan area, with roadside cafes for a rest stop

items.activity: Reach Kaeng Khut Khu before Chiang Khan town. Have lunch at a restaurant by the rapids, order kung ten (dancing shrimp) and grilled fish, and take in the rocky rapids midstream
items.note: In the low-water months (Feb–May) you can clearly see the rapids and sandbars. Restaurants and shops selling crispy coconut line the rapids

items.activity: Enter Chiang Khan town, check in to a guesthouse in the Chai Khong riverside area, drop your bags, and wander the old wooden houses
items.note: Many Chiang Khan guesthouses are century-old wooden houses converted to rooms, around 600–1,500 THB/night. They fill up fast in the cool season, so book ahead

items.activity: Cycle or stroll along the Mekong and stop at a riverside cafe for coffee while the heat eases off
items.note: Many guesthouses lend bikes for free, and the riverside road is easy to ride in the evening

items.activity: Walk the Chiang Khan walking street (Chai Khong Road), running from Wat Si Khun Mueang to Wat Tha Khok. Eat street food and buy the local crispy coconut
items.note: The market runs roughly 5 pm to 10 pm and the walk is about 1.5 km, with both food and souvenirs

items.activity: Dinner at a riverside restaurant. Try the old-recipe khao kha moo (stewed pork leg over rice) or river fish, and end the day with the lights on both banks of the Mekong
items.note: Popular spots on the walking street get long queues in the cool season, so leave time to wait or go before evening hits

blocks.text: Day 3 — Chiang Khan morning, up the mountains, then home

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Sticky-rice alms giving → Phu Tok → Loei mountains → drive home

items.activity: Wake early for the sticky-rice alms giving by the river, a ritual that happens every morning all along Chai Khong Road
items.note: Prepare sticky rice from your guesthouse or buy an alms set along the road. Sit on a mat and offer to the monks walking in a line. It's a morning scene the people of Chiang Khan really do every day

items.activity: Take a songthaew up Phu Tok to watch the sea of fog and the sunrise over Chiang Khan town and both banks of the Mekong
items.note: You have to take a local truck up Phu Tok, private cars can't go up. Parking is 20 THB and the ride up is 25 THB per person. It's busy in the cool season, so go up early

items.activity: Come down from Phu Tok, head back for breakfast in Chiang Khan town, then pack up and check out
items.note: Try khao piak sen (rice noodle soup) or old-style coffee at a place in town before you set off

items.activity: Drive inland into Loei and stop at a mountain spot, choosing Phu Pa Po or Suan Hin Pha Ngam depending on the time you have
items.note: Phu Pa Po is nicknamed the Fuji of Loei. You take a local truck up, with Phu Hor as the backdrop. If you have another night, you could push on to stay at Phu Ruea for the sea of fog

items.activity: Have lunch in Loei town or Dan Sai, then start the drive home
items.note: On the way back you can choose the inland route through Loei–Udon Thani back to Nong Khai, or retrace the riverside road. The inland route is faster

items.activity: Arrive in Nong Khai or Udon Thani and wrap up the cross-province trip
items.note: If you get back by evening, stop at a souvenir market to grab some Nong Khai pla som and naem to take home

items.name: Wat Pha Tak Suea + Skywalk
items.blurb: A cliffside temple in Sangkhom with a glass Skywalk jutting out from the rock, looking down on a bend in the Mekong. A morning spot for the sea of fog.

items.name: Than Thong Waterfall
items.blurb: A waterfall in the arboretum off Route 211, shady and good for a swim break on a long drive. It runs harder and looks better in the rainy season.

items.name: Kaeng Khut Khu
items.blurb: Rocky rapids in the Mekong just before Chiang Khan, with a sandy beach, restaurants by the rapids, and rows of crispy coconut for sale.

items.name: Phu Tok, Chiang Khan
items.blurb: A spot for the sea of fog and sunrise over Chiang Khan town. You take a local truck up for a panoramic view of both banks of the Mekong.

blocks.text: Adjusting the plan to your time

items: Only 2 days — combine days 1 and 2 into one, driving straight from Nong Khai to Chiang Khan, stopping at Wat Pha Tak Suea and Kaeng Khut Khu before overnighting in Chiang Khan. On day two, do the alms giving and Phu Tok, then head home
4 days to spare — add a night at Phu Ruea, go up Phu Ruea for the cool-season sea of fog, and stop at hilltop cafes and a vineyard before heading back
Going in the cool season — focus on the fog viewpoints: Wat Pha Tak Suea, Phu Tok and Phu Ruea, and set out before dawn each day to catch the fog
Going in the hot season — the Mekong is low and the rapids and sandbars show clearly, so focus on Kaeng Khut Khu, swimming at the waterfalls, and sitting at riverside restaurants

blocks.title: Rough budget
blocks.html: A self-drive trip of 3 days and 2 nights for two people runs about 4,000–6,000 THB. That breaks down to roughly 1,500–3,000 THB for two nights' lodging, 500–800 THB a day for food, around 1,200–1,800 THB for fuel round trip, and a few tens to a hundred baht in viewpoint entry fees. Souvenirs aren't included.

faq.q: How far is it from Nong Khai to Chiang Khan, and does it take long?
faq.a: Driving the Mekong riverside Route 211, it's about 200 km from Nong Khai town to Chiang Khan, roughly three and a half hours straight through. But we'd suggest leaving extra time to stop, since the sights are spread all along the way. That's why we lay it out as 3 days and 2 nights, with one night on the road in Sangkhom and one more in Chiang Khan.

faq.q: Can I do this route without my own car?
faq.a: You can, but it's a hassle. Public transport between Nong Khai, Sangkhom and Chiang Khan is limited, and stops like Wat Pha Tak Suea and the waterfalls are off the bus lines. The easier way is to rent a car and drive yourself from Nong Khai or Udon Thani. If you're going by bus, we'd suggest heading straight to Chiang Khan and focusing on the town itself.

faq.q: When is the best time to go?
faq.a: The cool season, November to February, is the best window: it's cool, with a good chance of a sea of fog at Wat Pha Tak Suea, Phu Tok and Phu Ruea. If you want to see the rocky rapids and sandbars in the Mekong clearly, go around February to May when the river drops.

faq.q: Where should I stay along the way?
faq.a: For the first night we'd suggest staying around Sangkhom, which has riverside places and homestays for about 600–1,500 THB. For the second night, stay in Chiang Khan around Chai Khong Road so you can walk the night market and easily get up for the morning sticky-rice alms giving. Book both ahead in the cool season, as they fill up fast.

faq.q: How should I prepare for the sticky-rice alms giving in Chiang Khan?
faq.a: Wake before 6 am and prepare sticky rice from your guesthouse, or buy an alms set sold along Chai Khong Road. Sit on a mat and wait for the monks to walk past in a line. It's a ritual the people of Chiang Khan genuinely do every morning, so dress modestly and take off your shoes as is the custom.
